title: endpoint-correlation-and-stream-fragment-logging-openai-shim
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Improve debuggability and metrics fidelity for streaming API calls and function/tool invocations while preserving OpenAI shim compatibility. Problem: when streaming tokens and invoking tools we were losing per-endpoint context and sequence information in logs and metrics (difficult to attribute errors and regressions). This PR introduces per-endpoint correlation ids, stream-fragment markers, and propagates trace+baggage into tool execution processes while mapping these fields into the OpenAI-compatible response surface.

What this change does (high level):
- Attach an endpoint-scoped correlation_id header (x-rw-correlation-id) to every API request and include it in structured access logs and JSONL streaming fragments.
- Emit stream fragment metadata with fields: fragment_id, seq_in_fragment, is_final, and fragment_offset to allow reassembly and per-fragment metrics.
- Propagate existing W3C traceparent and baggage headers into tool/function executor launches so tool logs include the same trace context.
- Add per-route metric labels (route_name, api_mode: streaming|non-streaming, compatibility: openai|native) so high-cardinality is controlled at metric emission layer.
- Maintain OpenAI shim compatibility: the OpenAI-compatible response still exposes id/request_id and the old headers (x-request-id) are populated from the new correlation id to avoid breaking downstream customers.

Checklist:
- [x] server: attach correlation id to request context and access logs
- [x] streaming: include fragment metadata in JSONL lines (prefixed with "rw-frag-" fields)
- [x] function/tool exec: set TRACECONTEXT and RW_BAGGAGE env vars before start
- [x] metrics: add per-route tags and a sanitizer to cap cardinality
- [x] tests: unit + integration test for reassembly and per-fragment metrics
- [x] docs: add small note to observability guide about fragment reassembly and header mapping

Commits summary: (high-level)
- feat(observability): add correlation_id middleware and header mapping
- feat(streaming): emit fragment metadata in streaming JSONL and update client shim
- feat(exec): propagate traceparent and baggage into tool subprocess env
- perf(metrics): add per-route label sanitizer and update metrics emitters
- test: add integration test for stream fragment ordering and metrics tagging
- docs: update observability guide and API compatibility section

Files changed (high-level):
- server/middleware/correlation.go (new middleware to generate/propagate correlation_id)
- api/streaming/fragment_emitter.go (stream fragment metadata attachment)
- adapters/openai/shim_response.go (map x-rw-correlation-id -> x-request-id and response.id)
- exec/launcher/launcher.go (inject tracing env into tool processes)
- metrics/route_labels.go (sanitizer for high-cardinality route tags)
- observability/docs/fragment-reassembly.md (docs)
- tests/integration/stream_fragments_test.go (integration tests)

Small illustrative example (what a streaming JSONL fragment now looks like):
{"rw_frag_fragment_id":"f0a9b2", "rw_frag_seq":1, "rw_frag_is_final":false, "content":"the quick brown"}
{"rw_frag_fragment_id":"f0a9b2", "rw_frag_seq":2, "rw_frag_is_final":true, "content":" fox jumps"}

Compatibility notes: the OpenAI shim will attach the following headers to preserve backwards compatibility: x-request-id (set from x-rw-correlation-id), and the response.id in non-streaming endpoints is set to correlation_id when an explicit request id is not present. No public API changes required for current customers using the OpenAI shim.

Testing and validation: added unit tests for correlation middleware, fragment ordering, and tool exec env propagation. Integration test runs a simulated streaming request with an invoked tool and asserts the logs emitted by the tool process contain the same traceparent and baggage.

Operational considerations:
- Per-route labels are sanitized to avoid explosion (we limit to well-known route_name set and fallback to 'custom' for unknown).
- Fragment IDs are UUID4-ish (short hash) and the fragment sequence numbers are small ints to avoid large telemetry cardinality.

Changelog/Release notes: Add per-endpoint correlation ids, streaming fragment metadata in logs, and trace propagation into function/tool execution. This improves troubleshooting for streaming+tooling flows and enables accurate per-route latency/error metrics.

review_comments: Marcus Cheng: Nice approach. Two asks: (1) ensure fragment ids are deterministic per request if retried; (2) add guard in metrics layer to avoid new high-cardinality labels.
Aisha Patel: Response: fragment ids are generated once per request and persisted in request context so retries reuse the same id; added sanitizer to metrics as requested.
Ivy Ramirez: Can we include a short example in the docs about reassembly? Also noticed launcher env var naming — prefer RW_TRACEPARENT to avoid env collisions.
Aisha Patel: Added example to docs and switched env var to RW_TRACEPARENT and RW_BAGGAGE per guidance.
Evan Liu: CI flake on nested integration test; re-ran and green. Approving pending small comment on logging formatting.
Aisha Patel: Addressed logging format comment (trim whitespace around JSONL fragments) and pushed fix.
release_notes: Add per-endpoint correlation IDs (x-rw-correlation-id) and streaming fragment metadata to JSONL logs; trace context now propagates into function/tool executors. OpenAI shim preserves x-request-id for compatibility. Improves observability for streaming+tooling flows.
notes_for_merger: Squash-merge after confirm no outstanding rollbacks. Metrics sanitizer added to avoid cardinality issues; operations has been notified and docs updated under observability guide.
